newsitem.title: USA: Clark sees alkylation unit up by Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Clark sees alkylation unit up by Thursday.

text.p: Clark Refining and Marketing said Wednesday that the alkylation unit at its Blue Island, Illinois refinery is expected to be back up by noon on Thursday, adding about 5,000 barrels per day to gasoline production.
The unit had been down since an October 19 fire, which also idled the plant's fluid catalytic cracker (FCC) and and a propane scrubber.
Clark said on November 14 that the FCC was brought back up and the plant was producing about two million gallons of gasoline a day. The alkylation unit will add about 210,000 gallons a day.

The restart of the alkylation unit had been delayed because Clark "found some additional maintenance work they wanted to do...in the process of getting it ready the first time around," said Syd Wiley, a spokesman for the plant.
The restart of the unit is expected to begin late Wednesday, with the unit back up fully by noon on Thursday, he added.

The restart of the idled units had been delayed until after an Illinois court ruled on November 8 on a lawsuit filed by the state's attorney requesting the whole plant be shut down pending a safety investigation.
The October 19 fire was the third major incident involving the refinery in two years. However, the court ruled that the refinery could go ahead and restart the downed units.
Clark Refining is a unit of Clark USA, which is controlled by Trizec-Hahn Corp of Toronto.
